basics.name: Raman Dhiman
basics.label: Ph.D. Candidate, McKetta Department of Chemical Engineering, UT Austin
basics.summary: Chemical engineer working at the intersection of membrane science, biophysics, and neuromorphic computing. I use droplet interface bilayer electrophysiology to build and characterize bio-membrane-based memristive materials for physical neuromorphic and reservoir computing.

Institute Silver Medal — second-highest cumulative performance index in the department

work.name: The University of Texas at Austin
work.summary: McKetta Department of Chemical Engineering. Advisors: Manish Kumar and Benny D. Freeman.
highlights: Characterize ion transport, selectivity, and voltage dependence in artificial lipid membranes using droplet interface bilayer electrophysiology, relating pore and peptide structure to conductance behavior.

Demonstrated the emergence of memristance in jammed interconnected bilayer emulsions using alamethicin, establishing that a 3D-printable tissue mimic reproduces voltage-dependent memory behavior (Nature Materials, 2026).

Showed that blocker molecules induce nonlinear conductance and emergent memristance in open pores that otherwise exhibit ohmic current–voltage behavior, extending memristive dynamics beyond voltage-gated channels (first-author, Faraday Discussions, 2026).
Developing more stable brain-mimicking bilayer networks and evaluating pore and peptide combinations for neuromorphic computing applications.
Contributed membrane characterization and electrophysiology to collaborative projects on lanthanide-selective artificial channels, dehydrated biomimetic membranes, and protective carbon fabrics.
Mentored eight graduate, undergraduate, and intern researchers; four are co-authors on peer-reviewed publications.

work.name: Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar
work.summary: Department of Chemical Engineering. Advisor: Kabeer Jasuja, Ph.D.
highlights: Synthesized and characterized boron-based nanosheets and studied their interaction with methylene blue dye in aqueous dispersion.
Resolved anomalous UV–visible spectra across a concentration matrix of nanosheets and dye, proposing that dye molecules aggregate in the presence of the nanosheets in addition to adsorbing onto them.
Presented at the 3rd International Conference on Soft Materials (ICSM 2018).
